text: Gene Filtering: First, lowly expressed genes removed, retaining genes expression level reaching min_count_threshold least min_gene_expressed samples. step based statistical power considerations, lowly expressed genes prone false-positive results differential analysis. Sample Filtering: Subsequently, low-quality samples filtered based three core indicators: Sequencing Depth: total number reads must reach min_total_reads. Library Complexity: number detected genes must exceed min_genes_detected. Sample Consistency: quality checking enabled, average correlation samples must meet min_correlation threshold. Data Integrity Check: Identifies technical anomalies; many missing values may indicate experimental issues. Feature Expression Filtering: Uses count threshold rather proportion threshold avoid -penalizing small samples. Genes must stably expressed multiple samples ensure reliability statistical tests. Sample-Level Filtering: Comprehensively evaluates technical quality: Sequencing depth ensures detection sensitivity, number detected genes reflects library diversity, sample correlation (Pearson) validates experimental reproducibility. PCA analysis identifies batch effects outlier samples. PCA Variance: Variance explained first two principal components. show_plot_results = TRUE, function generates PCA plot colored experimental condition Batch Effects: Proportion genes significantly affected batch

what: Find the Optimal Normalization Method for Seurat
title: Auxiliary Utils
text: simple scoring function selecting normalization method. Evaluates 3 dimensions preprocessing quality: Variance stabilization: Decoupling mean-variance relationship normalized expression (lower correlation = better). Biological signal retention: Preservation known marker genes within highly variable genes (higher retention = better). Dropout robustness: Removal technical dropout bias normalized values (lower correlation dropout rate = better). Exmaple Usage: Supports simultaneously adding Seurat objects preprocessed multiple methods, ensuring equivalent standard workflow NormalizeData + ScaleData + FindVariableFeatures.
code: obj <- Seurat::CreateSeuratObject(counts)  sct <- Seurat::SCTransfrom(obj) lognorm <- Seurat::NormalizeData(obj) %>%   Seurat::ScaleData() %>%   Seurat::FindVariableFeatures()  ChooseNormalization(   sct = sct,   lognorm = lognorm,   # * More can be added here   subset_size = integer(),   known_hvgs = list(),   n_hvgs = 2000L,   low_expressed_thresh = 0.2,   weight = c(     variance_stability = 0.4,     marker_signal = 0.35,     dropout_robustness = 0.25   ) ) # ℹ Using 1088 cells # ℹ Comparing 2 methods: sct and lognorm # ── Method Ranking (Composite Score) # Top method: log_norm # [1] log_norm: 0.825 # [2] sctransform: 0.175

what: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization
text: quantitative framework selecting optimal normalization strategies (e.g., SCTransform vs. LogNormalization) based diagnostic metrics rather heuristics. Evaluates three critical dimensions preprocessing quality: Variance stabilization: Decoupling mean-variance relationship normalized expression (lower correlation = better). Biological signal retention: Preservation known marker genes within highly variable genes (higher retention = better). Dropout robustness: Removal technical dropout bias normalized values (lower correlation dropout rate = better). Methods ranked using weighted composite score. Designed head--head comparison preprocessed Seurat objects.

title: Data-Driven Selection of Single-Cell Normalization Methods — ChooseNormalization

Number cells subsample diagnostics. missing empty, defaults min(10000, total_cells). Smaller subsets accelerate computation minimal accuracy loss large datasets (>50k cells). known_hvgs Named list canonical marker genes cell types. Format: list(cell_type1 = c("geneA", "geneB"), cell_type2 = c("geneC", ...)). Used compute marker_retention metric. NULL (default), metric omitted scoring. n_hvgs Integer. Number top highly variable genes evaluate marker retention. Default: 2000L. relevant known_hvgs provided. low_expressed_thresh Numeric (0–1). Quantile threshold filtering lowly expressed genes variance-mean correlation calculation. Genes quantile mean expression excluded. Default: 0.2 (bottom 20% excluded). weight Named numeric vector specifying weights composite scoring. Workflow: Identifies top marker genes per cluster (via Seurat::FindAllMarkers() user-provided markers). Queries specified LLMs marker gene lists tissue context. multiple models: computes consensus annotations uncertainty metrics (consensus proportion, entropy) via mLLMCelltype::interactive_consensus_annotation(). single model: uses direct annotation via mLLMCelltype::annotate_cell_types(). Adds results metadata columns Seurat object.
